paragraphs: Ekin Smart City Technology sells monitoring devices and software that law enforcement agencies use to enforce the laws of their communities. The product list runs from an Automatic License Plate Reader, or ALPR, to red light enforcement and speed and traffic enforcement. All of those devices feed data captured at the edge to maestro, the company's backend platform, which analyzes it in real time. Violations can then be issued automatically and monitored from a central dashboard.

One product, Ekin Patrol G2, is a modular AI-powered bar that attaches to vehicles, so a patrol car carries the sensors instead of fixed infrastructure. The company says it can detect and process speeding and parking violations in real time. It can also alert officers when someone approaches the vehicle. Ekin markets similar monitoring to neighborhoods, where the systems watch vehicles, pedestrian traffic and large wildlife around the clock in all weather.

Ekin designs and manufactures its own hardware and develops its software in-house. It states that it has used machine learning and artificial intelligence for more than 15 years. Both the law enforcement and neighborhood pages point to a case study of Coral Gables, Florida. A December 2025 press headline announces a $25M U.S. expansion and a transition to U.S.-based manufacturing.
